## Summary

Continues the staged migration of buyer-seller order communication toward NIP-17 encrypted, gift-wrapped messages.

This draft adds the library-level read pipeline in two reviewable layers:

1. A NIP-17 order-chat inbox read boundary.
2. Pairwise orchestration across legacy public order messages and NIP-17 messages.

This PR is stacked on and depends on #1136. It must not merge before #1136.

It does not complete the live application cutover.

## Stack and review order

1. #1136 — NIP-17 order read integration helper
2. `fb9e2919` — NIP-17 chat inbox read boundary
3. `055b6575` — NIP-17 chat read orchestration

Required merge order:

```text
#1136
  → this PR
  → later live-query, application, and publishing layers
```

Because #1136 and its child branches live in the contributor fork, GitHub’s comparison against upstream `master` is cumulative.

The narrow review ranges are:

```text
Layer 1:
075def1f6d5b47e32279a9bb65c36cadd7f4e135
  ..fb9e2919e9773e1a399f6f1eeb497f23c9a7538f

Layer 2:
fb9e2919e9773e1a399f6f1eeb497f23c9a7538f
  ..055b6575eab0d21cd098d5f13defa03796395309
```

## Layer 1: NIP-17 inbox boundary

Adds a dedicated boundary for reading and processing NIP-17 order-chat inbox events without coupling the protocol and domain layer to application queries or UI state.

The boundary:

- validates the active-user and optional counterparty identities;
- verifies that the signer remains bound to the active user;
- requires NIP-44 decryption support;
- resolves the active user’s configured NIP-17 relay list;
- fetches bounded gift-wrap candidates through an injected event-fetch dependency;
- treats relay, gift-wrap, seal, and rumor data as untrusted input;
- verifies and unwraps order-message rumors defensively;
- isolates malformed events and dependency failures;
- returns typed transport and domain records rather than NDK or UI objects.

Files:

```text
src/lib/orders/nip17OrderChatInbox.ts
src/lib/__tests__/nip17OrderChatInbox.test.ts
src/lib/nostr/nip17Relays.ts
src/lib/__tests__/nip17Relays.test.ts
```

## Layer 2: dual-read orchestration

Adds the orchestration boundary that reads legacy and NIP-17 sources independently and combines their authorized results.

The boundary:

- validates canonical lowercase 64-character participant keys;
- optionally validates that the supplied order context matches the participant pair;
- snapshots caller input, reader dependencies, and signer selection before invoking external callbacks;
- starts the legacy and NIP-17 reads concurrently;
- keeps source failures isolated and reports source health explicitly;
- normalizes and authorizes each candidate before deduplication;
- accepts only kind-14 order-chat rumors received through the NIP-17 source;
- requires exactly one recipient `p` tag for this order-chat boundary;
- verifies transport direction against the active user and counterparty;
- deduplicates by canonical inner message ID;
- prefers the authorized NIP-17 representation when legacy and NIP-17 records collide;
- preserves valid legacy-only records;
- sorts deterministically by `created_at`, then canonical event ID;
- provides structural order correlation without copying arbitrary subject text into correlation metadata.

Files:

```text
src/lib/orders/nip17OrderChatReadOrchestration.ts
src/lib/__tests__/nip17OrderChatReadOrchestration.test.ts
```

## Security and protocol boundaries

- Relay results are not trusted until validated.
- Signed legacy events and unsigned NIP-17 rumors remain distinct record types.
- Authentication and event-shape validation do not imply order-specific authorization.
- Gift-wrap and seal metadata are not treated as order-message domain tags.
- Authorization occurs before cross-source deduplication.
- An unauthorized or malformed candidate cannot suppress an authorized record with the same inner ID.
- Mutable caller input cannot replace the snapshotted readers or signer after source invocation begins.
- Failure results use fixed, non-sensitive metadata.
- Historical valid messages remain readable; this layer does not impose an artificial freshness cutoff.
- No payment, settlement, or fulfillment conclusion is inferred from chat-message presence.

## Non-goals

This PR intentionally does not include:

- `src/queries/orders.tsx` or other live query integration;
- React Query keys, cache invalidation, or polling behavior;
- checkout or order-chat UI wiring;
- application boot or state-management changes;
- storage or local-cache behavior;
- NIP-17 message construction, signing, wrapping, or publishing;
- removal of legacy kind `14`, `16`, or `17` reads or writes;
- an end-to-end product cutover;
- payment, settlement, or fulfillment-state derivation.

Later PRs can integrate these boundaries into live application reads and publishing after the protocol and authorization behavior is reviewed.

## Validation

Validation for the stacked implementation:

- Layer 1 focused tests: 48 passed, 0 failed; 203 assertions
- Layer 2 focused tests: 75 passed, 0 failed; 250 assertions
- Related NIP-17 and order-message suites: 157 passed, 0 failed; 706 assertions
- Full unit suite: 322 passed, 0 failed; 1,211 assertions across 21 files
- Prettier: passed
- Whitespace checks: passed
- NDK footprint: unchanged at 127 / 127
- TypeScript project diagnostics: byte-identical to the pre-existing baseline, with no diagnostics attributable to the added files
- E2E: not run; the approved validation scope excluded E2E and this PR adds no live query, UI, publishing, or application wiring

## Follow-up

Future PRs will integrate these read boundaries with live query and application behavior and, separately, with the NIP-17 publishing path.

Depends on #1136.  
Related to #1084.
